newsitem.title: DUBAI: Islamic group to send delegation to Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Islamic group to send delegation to Afghanistan.

text.p: The Organisation of the Islamic Conference said on Monday it would send a delegation to Afghanistan to push for an end to hostilities.
The mission would be led by the OIC's special representative for Afghanistan Ibrahim Bakr, the Saudi-based organisation said.

"The high-level OIC mission would meet with leaders of various Afghan parties and emphasise the need for an immediate cessation of armed hostilities and for political dialogue among all Afghan parties," the OIC said.
The radical Taleban movement seized the Afghan capital Kabul last month and imposed its strict reading of Islam on large areas of the country under its control.
On Monday the Taleban admitted for the first time it had lost key towns north of the capital to forces of former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
The OIC said Secretary General Hamid Algabid was closely monitoring the situation in Afghanistan.
"The secretary general has stated the OIC remains committed to working with the Afghan parties in helping to find a political solution to the conflict," the statement said.

"He reaffirmed that the OIC would continue to coordinate its efforts with the international community, in particular the United Nations, to promote peace, national reconciliation and reconstruction in Afghanistan."
The Jeddah-based OIC was founded in 1969 and groups more than 50 Islamic countries.
